hook: Jakub Pachocki joined OpenAI in 2017 as a theoretical computer scientist fresh from a PhD in convex optimization, and rose to run the research programs behind some of the company's largest bets, including GPT-4 and the reinforcement-learning system that beat the world Dota 2 champions. In May 2024 OpenAI named him Chief Scientist, succeeding Ilya Sutskever, putting him in charge of the company's core research direction. He is credited with helping steer OpenAI toward reasoning models that work through problems step by step, an approach that produced systems scoring at gold-medal level on the International Mathematical Olympiad. Sam Altman has called him one of the strongest research minds at the company.

standing.standing: Jakub Pachocki is Chief Scientist at OpenAI, a position he has held since May 2024, succeeding Ilya Sutskever, and he is in charge of the company's core research direction. He joined OpenAI in 2017 as a theoretical computer scientist and served as Director of Research before his promotion. He led research on GPT-4 and on OpenAI Five, the system that defeated the reigning Dota 2 world champions in 2019. He helped redirect OpenAI's research toward reasoning models, work that led to systems scoring at gold-medal level on the International Mathematical Olympiad. Sam Altman has called him one of the strongest research minds at the company, and he was named to TIME's 100 Most Influential People in AI in 2025.
